problem_type: Transient presentation ownership survives its interaction lifetime
symptom: Selected editable nodes intermittently lose the composer after history, interrupted drag, zero-sized layout or lazy failure. At default zoom, a large canvas node places composer parameter actions behind fixed bottom workspace docks. Editing B then confirming only A discarded B unsubmitted payment-card input. Frozen full audit also reproduced an unselected node history button doing nothing, canvas outer-card scrolling against its fixed-footer contract, and normal focus transfer cancelling a new primary pan. Real Electron video duration keyboard edits persisted but the visible slider stayed stale, and control arrow keys also moved the canvas node.
direct_cause: History has two state owners; boolean drag writes rediscover stage and reuse source identity; chunk errors reload the window; geometry can resolve to zero height in a nonzero stage. Reference hooks and prompt-library media also bypassed the host writer and modified canvas from panel. The panel writer ignored caller node identity and read current shot/scope after uploads settled; the same node could also belong to a refreshed quote or operation. Composer placement excluded the left dock but treated the full stage bottom as usable; its existing geometry watcher ignored bottom dock mounting and resizing. The newly bounded outer composer scroll card omitted the existing native React Flow nowheel region class; React synthetic stopPropagation alone does not provide that framework contract. Renderer revises only selected shots but cleared the entire two-layer draft after refresh/confirmation. The captured window blur listener accepted child-element blur events; its cancel callback cleared pointer start before movement. The history setter closed over selected=false although the visible trigger stops selection bubbling. The canvas card unconditionally enabled outer overflow-y-auto. Every React Flow position event, including keyboard movement outside a drag, disabled hasDefaultNodes and only populated a drag draft. Without drag-stop the ownership flag never recovered; batched projection updates stopped applying. Composer lacked the existing React Flow nokey scope. History open intent triggered its own invalidation effect while selected was still false in React Flow: domain selection updates pass through a passive projection effect and the framework batch. The synchronous selected-state harness had missed this intermediate render. The initial keyboard writeback also accepted late XYDrag position packets after cancellation; keyboard and mouse-end both carry dragging=false. Electron blur then mouseup reproduced a discarded position being saved and persistRevision incrementing. Final Electron v13 proved the duration panel portal escapes the composer DOM nokey ancestor while React synthetic keydown still bubbles to the node wrapper, moving the selected node by 5px during a valid slider edit.
class_root: Temporary UI state lacks a single owner tied to valid node, stage and gesture lifetimes. Shared composer content writes lacked explicit host-scoped authority. Asynchronous write authority was rebound to the currently displayed draft rather than the initiating editing visit. Usable-stage geometry must account for intersecting fixed workspace chrome through its existing owner. Framework input exclusion must follow each actual DOM interaction surface, including portals, rather than only the React component ancestor.

generality_proof: Every drag producer consumes the same stage-token lease primitive; all cancellation paths terminate that lease and producer state. History state is parent-controlled; both hosts reuse unchanged write access. Geometry and lazy behavior remain in existing owners. Composer usable-bottom calculation derives all marked workspace docks from the existing owner, not a toolbar class list; the existing geometry watcher includes their rectangles. Partial consumption expands the existing all layer into remaining per-shot effective patches and reuses the existing input-bound recovery key per remaining shot; only matching project/Run/operation/content/reference identities restore. No second storage owner. History intent invalidates on selection/availability/identity lifecycle changes, not on opening intent itself; delayed framework selection can therefore complete without discarding the original click. InlineParameterBar renders both single/multiple controls and canvas portal/payment inline surfaces through renderParameterPanel; each surface root supplies the installed framework nokey contract.

prevention.invariant: Lease ownership is captured at gesture start and cannot be reassigned by late cleanup.
prevention.failure_mode: Invalid origin acquires no stage; repeated release is a no-op; invalid history becomes closed.
prevention.strategy: Replace boolean/string release API with captured token lease, then close lifecycle exits at each producer. Bind panel writers to one editing visit and retire both read/write access on scope change or unmount; uploads stop after await when the captured writer is retired. Pending candidate projection supplies existing composer; host resolves explicit displayed shot identity against actual plan structure. Filter blur at the shared lease ingress by event target; keep selection acquisition at the existing history trigger and permit its captured opening intent without relying on the pre-selection closure; restore original scroll ownership. History invalidation uses lifecycle dependencies only, not openedFor. Non-drag position writeback requires the current synchronous React keydown dispatch; the installed RF still owns key filtering, selection and displacement. Out-of-lifetime pointer positions restore the current projection without an Undo/event/save. Reuse canvasDragWriteback for business commits, keeping the canvas shell below its existing limit. Parameter surface roots carry native framework nokey exclusion for both portal and inline modes; no synthetic keyboard algorithm or document-level handler is added.

legacy_paths.rationale: Remove stage fallback and owner-string clearing, and child-owned history state. No parallel overlay or reducer.

dependency_lifecycle.target: Existing React Flow renderer plus anchoredPlacement adapter
dependency_lifecycle.rationale: NodeToolbar source provides portal and inverse zoom but no measured flip/clamp. Replacement would remove required behavior. Installed @xyflow/react 12.11.5 NodeWrapper and NodesSelection use the same synchronous useMoveSelectedNodes → updateNodePositions → triggerNodeChanges → onNodesChange path. The adapter observes the native keydown eventPhase only during that dispatch; @xyflow/system isInputDOMNode excludes .nokey descendants, preserving control keyboard handling without replacing framework key, selection or movement logic.
exit_criteria: Revisit if placement requires virtual anchors, auto-placement or scrolling-container middleware; migrate whole owner with geometry and draft-preservation tests.

On React Flow or event integration upgrades, inspect the installed keyboard dispatch and .nokey implementations and rerun both node and multi-selection keyboard entry paths, composer slider edits without node movement, read-only refusal, cancelled pointer late-event zero-write behavior, single-Undo grouping and cold-restart persistence.

If keyboard position changes become asynchronous or .nokey stops excluding control events, the current eventPhase adapter is no longer valid: revise the shared adapter against the new framework contract and prove those regressions before retaining or upgrading it; do not widen the event lifetime with timers.
